claims.text: In-situ substrate preheating during additive manufacturing of AlCrFeNiSi will reduce residual thermal stresses.
In-situ substrate preheating will mitigate microstructural degradation in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi.
In-situ substrate preheating will simplify processing relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing regimes.
The proposed substrate-preheating target is approximately 500°C.
Processing requires an inert atmosphere.
The applicable substrate-preheating window is 400–600°C.
The approach applies to miniature components with cross-sectional feature sizes below or up to approximately 10 mm.
Rapid cooling and high thermal gradients occur in such miniature components under standard additive-manufacturing conditions.
Substrate preheating reduces the temperature gradient during layer deposition.
The reduced temperature gradient produces a slower cooling rate during layer deposition.
Slower cooling promotes more uniform grain growth.
Slower cooling reduces the formation of residual thermal stresses.
Moderating rapid-solidification effects refines the microstructure.
Reduced internal stress and refined microstructure enhance mechanical performance.
Preheated components will have greater microstructural uniformity than components produced without substrate preheating.
Preheated components will exhibit improved ductility relative to components produced without substrate preheating.
Preheated components will exhibit improved strength relative to components produced without substrate preheating.
Under conventional additive manufacturing without preheating, rapid cooling causes high residual stresses.
Under conventional additive manufacturing without preheating, rapid cooling degrades mechanical performance.
The results may not extend to larger components or other alloy systems.
